data.statement: Never `load --mode overwrite` the shared `memory` graph or `main` (it truncates the branch). Use a per-project graph (OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH=<project>) or a branch, and apply cluster changes via scripts/apply-cluster.sh, which snapshots and verifies the node count.

Deploy/rebuild the Omnigraph stack ONLY from Server/server/coding/mcp-servers/docker-compose.yml (canonical, Dockhand; binds 0.0.0.0:8090 for Caddy). Never rebuild it from agent-skills/infra/mcp-servers/docker-compose.server.yml — that dev variant binds 127.0.0.1 and shares the compose project name, so it clobbers the live viewer and takes omnigraph-ui.ohje.ooguy.com down.

Stateful container data (MinIO, DBs) must use an NVMe bind mount under $APPS_ROOT (/home/s/apps), NEVER a Docker named volume: the Semaphore prune-docker playbook runs `docker volume prune -f` every ~3 days and deletes any unreferenced named volume, wiping data whenever the stack is briefly down (this is what repeatedly wiped the Omnigraph graph).
Internet-exposed services sit behind Authelia SSO via the Caddy authelia snippet; no anonymous public access to management/memory APIs.

data.rationale: The main host home.pve.main (192.168.178.149; .153 is the retired OpenMediaVault VM address, same machine - identical TLS fingerprint on :8007) already runs Proxmox Backup Server. So the offsite copy is a PBS remote + scheduled sync job pulling into datastore 'offsite' on the offsite host, NOT a file copy: PBS sync is incremental, deduplicated and chunk-verified, and transfers only changed chunks, which is what makes a WAN link viable. The offsite box is normally powered off; the BIOS 'Power On By RTC Alarm' wakes it at 08:00, offsite-backup.service waits for the tailnet, runs every configured PBS sync job, then powers the machine off again - but only if nobody is using it. Reaching the main site REQUIRES tailscale --accept-routes because the homelab VMs are not tailnet peers; only OPNsense is, advertising 192.168.178.0/24. Main PBS fingerprint: 90:0F:F5:6E:D1:47:47:50:CD:15:61:CB:1C:D4:C8:64:88:64:AD:27:72:22:0E:63:76:0F:21:2E:81:D2:24:74
data.title: Offsite backups use a PBS remote + pull sync job, woken by BIOS RTC alarm at 08:00

data.rationale: The offsite host is an ASUS P8P67 EVO (Intel P67 chipset, i5-3450, BIOS 2012). P67 does not implement VT-d: there is NO DMAR ACPI table and /sys/kernel/iommu_groups is empty even with intel_iommu=on. GPU passthrough to a VM is therefore impossible - a hardware limit, not a configuration problem. A prior attempt (2026-02-08, setup-vm-passthrough.sh) bound the Radeon R9 290 to vfio-pci and blacklisted amdgpu/radeon, which left the GPU unusable by the HOST as well. Remediation: removed vfio.conf + gpu-blacklist.conf, stripped vfio from /etc/modules, cleaned the kernel cmdline, and added /etc/modprobe.d/amdgpu-hawaii.conf forcing amdgpu (kernel defaults are backwards for Hawaii/CIK: amdgpu cik_support=0, radeon cik_support=1, and radeon gives no Vulkan). Verified after reboot: 'Kernel driver in use: amdgpu', card0 with DP/DVI/HDMI and renderD128.
data.title: KDE Plasma runs directly on the offsite Proxmox host because the board has no VT-d

data.rationale: The offsite host exists to survive the main host dying, so a memory layer that only works while the main host is up would be useless there. It therefore takes the 'offline-capable client' role from agent-skills/infra/mcp-servers/omnigraph-setup/README.md: a local Omnigraph stack (server + MinIO; viewer omitted to save RAM on 8 GB) that agents always write to, reconciled with central by omnigraph-sync.sh under a device/<host> branch. The LOCAL bearer token is deliberately different from the CENTRAL one. Known gap: the local server's embedding provider is Ollama on cloud.vm, so semantic search degrades exactly when the main site is down; fix is a local Ollama with nomic-embed-text after the RAM upgrade.
data.title: Offsite host runs a local Omnigraph stack and syncs to central, rather than pointing at central

data.statement: Never attempt PCI/GPU passthrough on the offsite host (ASUS P8P67 EVO, Intel P67). The chipset has no VT-d: no DMAR ACPI table, zero IOMMU groups. Any vfio-pci/blacklist configuration there is not just useless but actively harmful - it takes the GPU away from the host too. Use the GPU on the host (amdgpu) instead. /root/scripts/setup-vm-passthrough.sh is renamed .DISABLED-no-iommu so it cannot be re-run.

The offsite host must run tailscale with --accept-routes=true. The homelab VMs are NOT tailnet peers; only OPNsense is, and it advertises 192.168.178.0/24. With RouteAll=false Tailscale reports 'connected' while the entire main site is unreachable, warning only via a health-check line. Re-running 'tailscale up' without --accept-routes silently turns it back off; verify with 'tailscale debug prefs | grep RouteAll'.

NetworkManager must never be installed on the offsite Proxmox host; it is pinned to priority -1 in /etc/apt/preferences.d/no-network-manager together with network-manager-* and plasma-nm. Proxmox manages vmbr0 via ifupdown2 and NetworkManager claims the same interfaces; if it wins, a host at a remote site drops off the network with no console to recover from. A stock 'apt install kde-plasma-desktop' pulls it in via plasma-nm's Recommends. Do NOT substitute --no-install-recommends: xserver-xorg is itself only a Recommends of kde-plasma-desktop.

On a Proxmox host running Docker, Docker sets the iptables FORWARD policy to DROP on every start, which silently kills networking for any VM on vmbr0. pve-bridge-forward.service (After=docker.service, PartOf=docker.service) re-inserts explicit ACCEPT rules for vmbr0 using an -C existence test so repeated runs cannot stack duplicates. Do not remove it.

Never replicate a Proxmox Backup Server datastore with rsync or any raw file copy. The .chunks tree and its index files are only consistent as a whole; a partially-synced datastore can look healthy and restore garbage. Use a PBS remote + sync job, which is incremental, deduplicated and chunk-verified.

The offsite host's auto power-off must never be a bare 'no user logged in' check. At boot there is never a session yet, so such a check powers the machine off seconds after someone presses the power button to use it as a desktop. offsite-backup-run.sh only considers shutdown inside the RTC wake window (07:45-10:00, matching the 08:00 BIOS alarm), waits GRACE_SECS=900 first, and then requires no login session AND no established SSH AND no attached herdr client. /etc/offsite-backup/no-shutdown disables power-off entirely.

data.title: Create an API token on home.pve.main PBS and add it as a remote on the offsite host, then create the sync job and remove /etc/offsite-backup/no-shutdown

data.location: uid 1001, no sudo, home on ZFS dataset old/home-guest at /home/guest (~284 GB); Steam installed via steam-installer + i386 multiarch
data.name: guest account on the offsite host (browsing + gaming)

data.statement: KDE Plasma System Monitor cannot display AMD GPU usage on Debian 13: libksysguard ships only ksysguard_plugin_nvidia.so and has no AMD backend, so no configuration will make it work. This is a monitoring gap, NOT the GPU being unused - verify with 'glxinfo -B' (expect Accelerated: yes, radeonsi/hawaii) and /sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_busy_percent under load. Use nvtop (supports amdgpu, per-process) or radeontop instead. An idle desktop on an R9 290 genuinely reads ~0%, so CPU activity with a flat GPU is expected while browsing.

On the offsite host the root filesystem is a 26 GB LVM volume on a 32 GB USB flash stick. Every directory that grows without bound must live on the ZFS pool as its own dataset, never on root: /var/lib/vz (old/vz), /root/code (old/code), /var/lib/docker (old/docker), /var/cache (old/varcache), /mnt/datastore/offsite (old/pbs), the Omnigraph MinIO store (old/omnigraph-data) and /home/guest (old/home-guest, Steam libraries). Moving /var/lib/docker requires stopping docker first; moving /home wholesale requires no live KDE session.

Installing proxmox-backup-server adds /etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources, which returns 401 Unauthorized without a subscription and makes every subsequent 'apt update' fail. Set Enabled: false on it, exactly as with pve-enterprise.sources and ceph.sources. Use the pbs-no-subscription and pve-no-subscription repos instead.

data.rationale: The offsite host doubles as a desktop. Browsing and Steam run as 'guest' (uid 1001, NOT in sudo) so casual use has no path to root on a machine that is also a hypervisor and a backup target; 'maulser' (uid 1000, in sudo) stays the admin account and root cannot log into KDE at all. guest's home is the ZFS dataset old/home-guest mounted at /home/guest, because the root filesystem is a 26 GB LVM volume on a USB stick and a single Steam title would fill it. Steam needs dpkg --add-architecture i386 plus the non-free component, and mesa-vulkan-drivers:i386 for 32-bit RADV on the R9 290.
data.title: Separate unprivileged 'guest' account for browsing and gaming, with its home on ZFS

data.location: mirror of ata-ST16000NM000J-2TW103_ZR5F8YSG + _ZR5F8GRN; ashift=12, lz4, 14.5 TiB usable; dataset offsite/pbs -> /mnt/datastore/offsite
data.name: ZFS pool 'offsite' - 2x16TB mirror on the offsite host

data.rationale: The two Seagate Exos X18 drives installed in the offsite host (ZR5F8YSG, ZR5F8GRN, 14766 power-on hours each) still carried ZFS labels naming them members of the MAIN homelab's 'media' raidz1 (hostname 'home', the 4-disk pool holding the 44 TiB vm-102-disk-0 zvol behind OpenMediaVault). Two of the four members were absent, so the pool was UNAVAIL and nothing could be recovered from these disks alone. The wipe was explicitly authorised - the media pool is retired. Built as a MIRROR rather than a stripe: this machine's entire purpose is being the surviving copy when the main host dies, so surviving a single disk failure is the point. The PBS datastore moved from old/pbs (a 320 GB 5400 rpm laptop disk) onto offsite/pbs, 14.4 TiB free.
data.title: Offsite backup pool built as a 2x16TB mirror from the retired 'media' raidz1 disks

data.rationale: The host was observed suspending itself. A suspended Proxmox host drops off the tailnet, stops answering PBS syncs, and is indistinguishable from a crashed one when viewed from the far end of a tunnel - on a machine at a site nobody can walk to. All five sleep targets (sleep, suspend, hibernate, hybrid-sleep, suspend-then-hibernate) are masked, so even KDE PowerDevil's request fails rather than succeeding quietly, plus /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/00-no-sleep.conf sets every lid/idle/power-key handler to ignore and IdleAction=ignore. Screen blanking still works; deliberate poweroff via the RTC wake cycle is unaffected because systemctl poweroff is not a sleep target.
data.title: The offsite host must never suspend - all sleep targets masked

data.statement: Creating a Proxmox Backup Server API token is only HALF the job. PBS tokens start with Privilege Separation enabled and inherit nothing from their user, so a token can authenticate perfectly (/api2/json/version returns 200) while /api2/json/access/permissions returns {} and /api2/json/admin/datastore returns [] - which looks identical to 'the server has no datastores'. Always grant an explicit ACL: Configuration > Access Control > Permissions > Add > API Token Permission, path /datastore, role DatastoreReader, Propagate on. Verify by checking that access/permissions stops returning {}.

omnigraph-setup/setup-sync.sh schedules via a `systemd --user` timer. When run as a user with no user session (root over SSH), it logs 'no systemd --user session; falling back to cron' and then INSTALLS NOTHING - the crontab is left with only its comment header, and the script still exits 0 reporting success. Always verify the schedule actually exists after running it. On the offsite host the schedule is defined as ordinary SYSTEM units instead: omnigraph-sync.service + omnigraph-sync.timer (OnBootSec=5min, OnUnitActiveSec=15min, Persistent=true).

Duplicate EDGES in an Omnigraph graph can only be removed on the memory SERVER host (coding.vm), because the fix requires a store reset on the MinIO volume - scripts/dedup-graph.py. A client host cannot do it. When central has duplicate edges the client sync's verify gate refuses to push into or pull from that graph; this is CORRECT behaviour protecting the clean local copy, not a failure. As of 2026-08-16 the central homelab-server graph has 3 duplicate edges blocking sync of that one graph from the offsite host; all other graphs sync normally.

data.rationale: Measured live during a real sync: 3.6 MiB/s (~30 Mbit/s) between the offsite host and home.pve.main, with the Tailscale path DIRECT (41 ms, not DERP-relayed) - so this is the main site's upstream, not a tunnel problem. The source datastore 'backup' holds 7.52 TiB of 10.22 TiB, which at that rate is ~25 days for a full seed; host/cloud-share alone (~2 TiB, a daily 1.9 TiB cloud.pxar file-level backup) is ~6.7 days. That is incompatible with the wake-at-00:00-sync-then-power-off model. Incremental syncs are fine - PBS transfers only changed chunks - so ONLY the initial seed is the problem. Sync job offsite-pull is therefore created with --rate-in 1250000 (10 Mbit/s, leaving ~2/3 of the link for everything else at both sites), --group-filter type:vm (excluding the file share) and --transfer-last 3 (vm/100 alone has 98 snapshots and full history buys no disaster-recovery benefit), with NO schedule, plus /etc/offsite-backup/hold-sync as a second brake. Best long-term fix is to seed locally over gigabit LAN and relocate the box.
data.title: Offsite PBS seed is held and rate-limited to 10 Mbit/s; a full seed cannot cross the WAN link

data.statement: The offsite host's unattended-wake window must be evaluated against the BOOT time, captured before any work starts - never against the clock after the sync finishes. The first full pull runs for hours, so evaluating afterwards makes a normal scheduled wake look like a mid-morning human boot, and the machine never powers itself off. offsite-backup-run.sh captures START_HHMM at start-up. The window also crosses midnight now that the BIOS RTC alarm is 00:00 (23:50-02:00), which in_window() handles explicitly, and the values must use 10# prefixes so 0000/0750 are not parsed as octal.

Two traps when restore-testing from a PBS datastore. (1) PBS_FINGERPRINT must be the FULL 32-byte colon-separated hash; a truncated value fails as 'certificate validation failed - Certificate fingerprint was not confirmed', which reads like a TLS problem rather than a copy-paste one - extract with grep -oE '([0-9a-f]{2}:){31}[0-9a-f]{2}'. (2) Cancelling a sync mid-flight leaves *.tmp files and no index.json.blob in the snapshot directory, and the next verify fails on it; delete the snapshot directory and let garbage collection reclaim the chunks. Restoring as root@pam needs a password, so generate a local API token (proxmox-backup-manager user generate-token) and grant it DatastoreAdmin on the datastore.

As of 2026-08-16 the main PBS datastore 'backup' contains 8 VM groups and one file share (host/cloud-share) but NO backup of the Proxmox host's own configuration - there is no host/<pve-hostname> group. /etc/pve (guest configs, storage.cfg, user.cfg, firewall), /etc/network/interfaces and the ZFS pool layout are absent, so VM disks alone cannot rebuild the hypervisor: storage and network definitions would have to be reconstructed by hand. Fix by running on the main host: proxmox-backup-client backup etc.pxar:/etc --backup-type host --backup-id pve-config. It is a few MB, so it costs nothing over the link. Also note VM 102 (OpenMediaVault) is not backed up at all, and vm/107's last backup is 2026-06-21 - either decommissioned or a silently failing job.

data.title: Add a host-level PBS backup of /etc (and /etc/pve) on the main Proxmox host so the offsite copy can rebuild the hypervisor, not just the VMs
Decide and execute the initial PBS seed: local gigabit seed then relocate, or a scoped VM-only pull over the rate-limited WAN link
Check why vm/107's last PBS backup is 2026-06-21 - decommissioned or a silently failing backup job

data.rationale: The OpenMediaVault VM (102) is legacy and has been removed. NFS and Samba shares are now provided by the main Proxmox host itself rather than by a NAS guest. Consequences: (a) VM 102 missing from the PBS backup groups is NOT a gap and should not be filed as one; (b) the export and share definitions now live in the main host's own /etc, which makes a host-configuration backup materially more important - losing /etc now loses the file-server configuration as well as the hypervisor's storage and network definitions; (c) documentation that describes omv-vm/.153 as an OpenMediaVault NAS is stale - .153 is an address of home.pve.main, verified by identical TLS fingerprint on :8007.
data.title: VM 102 (OpenMediaVault) removed; NFS and Samba are now served directly by the main Proxmox host

data.location: Server/Proxmox-offsite/backup-host-config.sh + host-config-backup.{service,timer}; captures etc.pxar:/etc, etcpve.pxar:/etc/pve and a generated inventory.pxar
data.name: Host-configuration backup to PBS (backup-host-config.sh)

data.statement: Writing a backup to a Proxmox Backup Server datastore requires the Datastore.Backup privilege. Datastore.Read, Datastore.Audit and Datastore.Verify are sufficient to PULL (a sync job) but NOT to write, and the failure only appears once the backup protocol has already started: 'Error: missing permissions Datastore.Backup on /datastore/backup'. Prefer a SEPARATE push-only token from the pull token, especially when the credential lives on a machine at another site.

Two pxar traps when backing up a Proxmox host's own config. (1) /etc/pve is a FUSE mount of the cluster config DB; pxar does not cross into it while archiving /etc, so it must be listed as its own archive (etcpve.pxar:/etc/pve) or the guest configs, storage.cfg, user.cfg and firewall rules are silently absent from the backup. (2) pxar archives a DIRECTORY, not a file - writing a generated inventory into a shared scratch dir such as /var/tmp and archiving that path sweeps up everything else living there. Give generated content its own directory (/var/lib/host-inventory).

Server/Proxmox-offsite/etc-snapshot/ is pushed to a public GitHub repo, so collect-config.sh redacts credentials rather than copying them - /etc/proxmox-backup/remote.cfg carries a plaintext 'password' line. The leak check must assert that every credential-looking line CARRIES the <REDACTED> marker, not try to pattern-match what a secret looks like: an earlier version matched [^<] after the key/separator and the regex backtracked over the space, flagging an already-redacted line as a leak. etc-snapshot/ is reference-only and must NEVER be installed onto a host - restoring another machine's /etc/network/interfaces is how a remote host gets stranded; the separate etc/ directory is the one install.sh deploys.

data.title: Grant Datastore.Backup on the main PBS, then enable host-config-backup.timer on the offsite host and add the equivalent job on the main Proxmox host

data.statement: The offsite host's BIOS RTC runs in UTC (timedatectl: 'RTC in local TZ: no'), so the BIOS 'Power On By RTC Alarm' is a UTC time: an alarm set to 00:00 fires at 00:00 UTC = 02:00 CEST in summer and 01:00 CET in winter. The unattended-wake window in offsite-backup.service MUST therefore be expressed in UTC and START_HHMM captured with 'date -u'. On 2026-08-17 the window was 23:50-02:00 in LOCAL time, the box woke at 02:00:58 CEST and logged 'boot at 0201 is outside the unattended window ... staying up' - 58 seconds outside - so it stayed powered on all night with nothing to do. A local-time window also breaks silently at every DST change. When changing the BIOS alarm, set the window to the same UTC time, not the local time shown on screen.
